news.title: STAT+: At MAHA Summit, a grassroots movement goes corporate
news.summary: Federal officials and health care executives rubbed elbows at the ritzy MAHA Summit, causing some supporters to question what MAHA has become.

news.title: STAT+: Lawmakers urge Trump to rethink new rule that could restrict imported meds from Canada and overseas
news.summary: Some lawmakers are urging the Trump administration to rethink a pending rule that may prevent Americans from obtaining medicines from licensed international pharmacies.

news.title: STAT+: PhRMA taps Eric Cantor as new CEO
news.summary: Eric Cantor, a former GOP House majority leader, is taking the helm of PhRMA at a challenging time for the industry.

news.title: STAT+: Beam Therapeutics sues Chinese biotech, VC-backed startup, alleging theft of intellectual property
news.summary: The gene-editing company Beam Therapeutics is alleging that one of its scientists stole intellectual property and used it to co-found a Chinese company that made a deal with VC firms.

news.title: STAT+: Overton won’t get a vote before midterms
news.summary: Health department nominees await Senate votes, and we map out what the elections mean for healthy policy.

news.title: STAT+: Anthropic joins ARPA-H clinical AI moonshot, will hold closed-door health care event
news.summary: In this edition of STAT Health Tech: Oura delays IPO plans, Anthropic joins an clinical AI effort by ARPA-H, and MAHA's health data goals.

news.title: STAT+: AstraZeneca invests $2 billion in Summit Therapeutics
news.summary: AstraZeneca is teaming up with Summit Therapeutics to test its PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab alongside AstraZeneca’s antibody-drug conjugates.

news.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about Novo licensing a Chinese obesity pill, Merck pulling an antibiotic, and more
news.summary: Novo has agreed to pay up to $2.6 billion to license an experimental, weekly weight loss pill from China’s Hengrui Pharma

news.title: Researchers slow neurodegeneration in mice by barring T cells from the brain
news.summary: A new study in mice led by Washington University in St. Louis researchers suggests that stopping certain immune cells from entering the brain could limit neurodegeneration.

news.title: STAT+: UniQure’s gene therapy continues to slow Huntington’s progression after four years
news.summary: UniQure's gene therapy continues to slow Huntington's progression after four years. But the magnitude of the benefit waned compared to a similar analysis from a year ago.

news.title: Why MAHA wants to make health data much more accessible
news.summary: At a MAHA Institute event, Kennedy and others argued that health data should be more accessible to researchers can study vaccines, chronic diseases, and autism

news.title: She’s spent two decades talking to parents who don’t vaccinate their children. Here’s what she’s learned
news.summary: Jennifer Reich has spent two decades speaking to families about their immunization decisions. In an interview, she unpacks what she's learned.

news.title: STAT+: The last ‘breakthrough’ devices to get special treatment from Medicare
news.summary: New medical devices deemed "breakthrough" by the FDA are no longer automatically eligible for extra Medicare payments.

news.title: STAT+: Drug pricing, Medicaid, and research funding: The key policy issues at stake in the midterms
news.summary: Big shifts in health care policy could emerge depending on who wins the midterms, affecting hospitals and pharma companies.

news.title: Opinion: Child health is the national security crisis we keep ignoring
news.summary: “National security begins in childhood,” write Tina L. Cheng, Stanley McChrystal, and James M. Perrin.

news.title: Waltz Health, Fresenius Kabi partner for direct-to-payer biosimilar program
news.summary: Digital health company Waltz Health is teaming up with drugmaker Fresenius Kabi to support direct-to-employer efforts for key biosimilar medications.

news.title: Elevance Health rolls out new site-of-care billing policies
news.summary: Elevance Health is rolling out new billing policies that aim to ensure services are paid for at the appropriate level and drive greater transparency into where patients receive care.

news.title: Midwest nonprofits HealthPartners, Essentia Health announce merger plans
news.summary: The deal would yield a roughly $12.5 billion, multi-state integrated nonprofit with 22 hospitals and a 1.6 million-member insurance business.

news.title: Health tech's dealmaking boom is back as firms chase scale and profitable growth
news.summary: Health tech and digital health M&A activity remains a major force in 2026, driven by strategic expansion and the race for competitive artificial intelligence capabilities.

news.title: EliseAI banks $350M, hits $4B valuation for accelerated new product development
news.summary: The company surpassed $200 million in ARR in June, doubling revenue year-over-year for five consecutive years, executives said.

news.title: Smart ring maker Oura postpones public listing due to 'uncertainty in the IPO market'
news.summary: Smart ring maker and health tracking company Oura is postponing its previously announced initial public offering on Nasdaq due to "uncertainty in the IPO market," the company announced Tuesday morning.

news.title: CMS projects Medicare Advantage premiums to decline by 16% in 2027
news.summary: The Trump administration is projecting significant declines in premiums for Medicare Advantage plans in 2027.

news.title: Memorial Hermann CEO set to retire at the end of this year
news.summary: Memorial Hermann Health System's CEO, David Callender, will retire at the end of the year, the health system announced Monday.

news.title: SCAN expands reach into Oregon in partnership with the Springs Living
news.summary: SCAN Health Plan is teaming up with the Springs Living, a senior living organization, to launch new co-branded products that aim to offer a more connected experience for people living in these communities.

news.title: UnitedHealthcare, TeamHealth settle $100M fraud suit in Tennessee
news.summary: A 2021 legal battle between UnitedHealthcare and TeamHealth was dismissed after the parties reached a settlement, per court documents.

news.title: Chutes & Ladders—UnitedHealthcare names president; Joint Commission CEO to retire
news.summary: Welcome to this week's Chutes & Ladders, our roundup of hirings, firings and retirings throughout the industry. Please submit the good news—or the bad—from your shop, and we will feature it here at the end of each week.

news.title: OpenEvidence partners with Anthropic, Penn Medicine to expand physician access to AI across Africa and Asia
news.summary: OpenEvidence is teaming up with Anthropic to expand its artificial intelligence-powered clinical decision support technology to physicians in low- and middle-income countries across Africa and Asia.

news.title: Canadian $5M accelerated clinical trial program cuts start-up to 45 days
news.summary: A newly launched $5 million clinical trial program allows clinical trial sponsors to start trials in as little as 45 days in Ontario.

news.title: Enanta sheds staffers as key antiviral, immunology readouts loom
news.summary: As antiviral specialist Enanta Pharmaceuticals endeavors to expand into immunology, the company has decided to lay off 37 employees, Fierce has learned.

news.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Enanta sheds staffers; BMS slashes 265 HQ roles
news.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

news.title: uniQure stock crashes as Huntington’s gene therapy data weaken
news.summary: uniQure’s Huntington’s disease gene therapy has failed to significantly slow disease progression after 48 months, sending the biotech’s stock down 41% when trading began. But mitigating circumstances and the ongoing strength of a secondary endpoint kept analysts optimistic about AMT-130’s path to approval.

news.title: ai3Bio emerging from stealth to ‘take the gun out of the hands of the immune system’
news.summary: ai3Bio has emerged from stealth with $48 million in funding and a buzzing platform for targeting T cells in autoimmune disease.

news.title: Novo agrees $2.6B deal for preclinical GLP-1/GIP drug from in-demand Hengrui
news.summary: Novo’s ongoing efforts to rejuvenate its pipeline have seen the Big Pharma turn to one of the most in-demand drug developers in China.

news.title: AstraZeneca scales Summit’s PD-1xVEGF strategy with $2B investment to fuel ADC combos
news.summary: AstraZeneca is investing $2 billion in Summit Therapeutics to accelerate the development of PD-1xVEGF bispecific ivonescimab in combination with antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The newly minted partners will start by testing ivonescimab with AstraZeneca’s CLDN18.2-directed ADC in gastrointestinal cancers.

news.title: Roche drops muscle-sparing obesity antibody after flunked interim analysis
news.summary: Roche has slammed the brakes on an obesity antibody after the candidate showed little hope of hitting its endpoints in a phase 2 study.

news.title: Mirum posts phase 3 hepatitis win for ‘commercially differentiated’ challenger to Gilead, Vir
news.summary: A phase 3 trial of Mirum Pharmaceuticals’ chronic hepatitis delta virus drug candidate has hit its primary endpoint, furthering the biotech’s efforts to enter a space recently colonized by Gilead Sciences.

news.title: Scynexis bags $214M BARDA contract for antifungal development
news.summary: The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) has awarded Scynexis a $214 million contract for the development of a treatment for invasive fungal infections.

news.title: Tolerance continues thymus-focused deals with $560M pact for Tanabe's clinical-stage IL-33 drug
news.summary: After vaulting into the clinic by licensing a fusion protein last month, Tolerance Bio has continued to strengthen its thymus-focused pipeline by picking up an anti-IL-33 drug from Tanabe Pharma.

news.title: Precision Neuroscience taps $250M in Series D funding for brain-computer interface
news.summary: Precision Neurosciences, which specializes in brain-computer interface technology, raised $250 million in an oversubscribed Series D financing round.

papers.title: Omni-Decision: Evidence-Ledger Planning for Omni-Modal Agents
papers.summary: Omni-modal agents must seek evidence across video, audio, web pages, and computation to answer questions. Their main bottleneck is planning: noisy multimodal observations accumulate in conversation history and disrupt later decisions, while multimodal models have limited capacity for multi-step planning. Controlled backend replacements support this diagnosis: replacing the planner causes a much larger performance loss than replacing the perception backend. papers.title: Preference-Guided Adaptation for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Prompt Disagreement
